messages:
cheng: Quick follow-up — we need clarity on adapter interface for hosted/dedicated/private, specifically credential ownership when private sidecars are in customer VPCs. Do we expect control plane to hold creds, or runtime/sidecar to be the authority? cc @maria

maria: short answer: two patterns. (1) Control-plane-managed tokens (short-lived): simpler for hosted but requires network egress from private. (2) Customer-managed KMS + runtime fetch/callback: better for air-gapped, more ops on customer side.

alex: +1 to listing tradeoffs. Also need to call out audit + rotation. If control plane issues tokens we need token binding to session id and clear TTL. How will rollback work on fallbacks?

anya: idea: add `credential_scope` to manifest and a small handshake that declares `requires_egress: true|false`. Example manifest snippet:
```
{"adapter_version":"v2","credential_scope":"control-plane|customer-kms","requires_egress":false}
```
Runtime reads and enforces: if requires_egress==false, control plane MUST NOT store long-lived secrets. If control-plane mode used, enforce ephemeral creds only.

sam: infra question — for customer-kms mode where runtime fetches from customer KMS, who handles retries and rate limiting? if control plane proxies requests we reintroduce risk. I'd prefer runtime fetch with client cert auth to KMS.

maria: agree. Add two more fields: `credential_fetch_endpoint` (optional) and `fetch_auth_method` (e.g., 'mutual_tls'|'signed_request'|'none'). That keeps surface explicit.

alex: also surface observability: token issuer id in telemetry, rotation events as structured traces. We must avoid putting raw secrets into logs by accident.

deploy-bot: infra-rfc branch created: https://git.company/repo/pulls/241 — CI lint ok :white_check_mark:

cheng: ok actionable: maria to draft RFC with manifest changes + handshake flow; sam to write runtime fetch flow and failure modes; alex to write observability/rotation tracing spec. I'll schedule 30m sync Thurs. thanks everyone :rocket:
